scheme_name: Infrastructure Development Scheme for MSME Clusters
overview: The Infrastructure Development Scheme for MSME Clusters aims to support the sustainability and growth of micro and small enterprises by addressing common issues such as technology, skills, quality, and market access. It focuses on creating and upgrading infrastructural facilities in industrial areas and clusters, setting up Common Facility Centres for testing, training, raw material depot, effluent treatment, and complementing production processes. The scheme promotes green and sustainable manufacturing technology and supports infrastructure development projects including flatted factory complexes.
objectives: To support the sustainability and growth of MSEs by addressing common issues such as improvement of technology, skills & quality, market access, etc.
To create/upgrade infrastructural facilities in the new/existing Industrial Areas/Clusters of MSEs.
To set up Common Facility Centres (for testing, training, raw material depot, effluent treatment, complementing production processes, etc).
Promotion of green & sustainable manufacturing technology for the clusters.
Creation of Common Facility Centers including Plug & Play Facilities.
Support for Infrastructure Development Projects including Flatted Factory Complexes.
eligibility: Existing Entrepreneurs [in form of a Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs)].
benefits: GoI Assistance: up to 80% of the maximum Project cost of Rs. 30 crores. Creation of, “Tangible Assets” such as Common Production / Processing Centre, Design Centers, Testing Facilities including Plug & Play Facilities.
financial_support: GoI Assistance: up to 80% of the maximum Project cost of Rs. 30 crores. The scheme provides financial assistance for infrastructure development, common facility centres, and technology upgradation in MSME clusters.
application_process: 1. Identify the cluster and form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV). 2. Prepare a detailed project report including infrastructure needs, common facility requirements, and technology upgradation plans. 3. Submit the application through the Implementing Agency (State/Central Govt. organizations, NGOs) who need to provide land and 10% (5% in NER, J&K and Hill Areas) of Hard Intervention. 4. The Implementing Agency will forward the application to the Office of Development Commissioner (MSME) for scrutiny. 5. Upon approval, financial assistance of up to 80% (95% in NER, J&K and Hill Areas) of Hard Intervention cost, entire cost of Soft Intervention, Technical Agency fee and Implementing Agency fee is given by GoI.
caveats: Financial assistance of up to 80% (95% in NER, J&K and Hill Areas) of Hard Intervention cost.
Entire cost of Soft Intervention, Technical Agency fee and Implementing Agency fee is given by GoI.
Artisans are constituted into Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) by Implementing Agencies who need to provide land and 10% (5% in NER, J&K and Hill Areas) of Hard Intervention.
